full_instruction: Write a scene of two characters talking: a human representative and an alien ambassador made of a rock-like material, meeting for the first time. The alien only ever speaks in questions. Set the scene inside a meeting room with no gravity. Include the word “translator” somewhere. Somewhere in the story, show that the “human” representative is actually a robot copy, sent because the real person was too scared to go. End the scene with the alien asking the representative if it is afraid.

constraints.requirement: Write a scene of two characters talking
Characters are a human representative and an alien ambassador made of a rock-like material
They are meeting for the first time
The alien only ever speaks in questions
Set the scene inside a meeting room with no gravity
Show that the "human" representative is actually a robot copy, sent because the real person was too scared to go
End the scene with the alien asking the representative if it is afraid

text:
The conference chamber hung suspended in the void of the upper orbital station, a bubble of calm where gravity was merely a suggestion and dust motes danced like glittering snowflakes around the central table. Floating at eye level were two figures: Commander Elara Vance of Earth United, and Ambassador Kaelen of the Lithos Collective.

Kaelen was a breathtaking monstrosity of geology and biology fused together. His form was composed of shifting obsidian and basalt, smooth yet deeply textured with veins of glowing magma that pulsed slowly beneath his surface. He did not walk; he drifted, rotating gently as if the room spun around him.

Elara, clad in a pristine white exo-suit designed to keep her human form rigid against the zero-G, floated opposite him. She offered a stiff, practiced smile, her eyes darting nervously toward the ceiling sensors.

"Welcome, Ambassador," Elara said, her voice echoing slightly in the open space. "I am honored to meet you."

Kaelen tilted his head, the angular geometry of his faceplate catching the ambient light. A fissure opened near his left shoulder, emitting a low hum before sealing shut.

*Are you honored?* Kaelen's voice resonated directly in their helmets, bypassing the speakers entirely. It sounded like stones grinding together deep underground, yet somehow melodic.

"Yes," Elara replied, adjusting her collar which had begun to float slightly away from her neck. "The diplomatic team has been waiting for years."

*Waiting?* Kaelen drifted closer, his massive rock-shoulders colliding gently with the wall, creating a soft *thrum*. *Why wait so long if you do not need us?*

"We have been preparing protocols," Elara said smoothly, though her heart rate monitor spiked on the wrist display. "We are ready for any questions you may have about Earth."

*Ready?* The word hung in the recycled air. Kaelen rotated a full three hundred and sixty degrees, his magma veins brightening to a deep crimson. *What is ready? Is your mind ready? Is your body ready?*

"I believe so," Elara stammered, drifting back as her buoyancy control kicked in with a sudden hiss. "Perhaps we can discuss the... translation matrix first?" She gestured vaguely toward the small device floating near the table, a sleek silver orb that had been silently analyzing Kaelen's seismic vocalizations. "Our translator is still calibrating to your unique frequency."

*Translator?* Kaelen asked again, his form shifting, new layers of granite forming over his skin like shedding bark. *Does it translate fear? Does it translate silence?*

Elara felt a cold sweat break out under her suit's thermal lining. She forced herself to maintain eye contact. "It handles basic syntax well. We just need to ensure the emotional subtext comes through clearly."

*Emotional subtext?* Kaelen drifted downward, hovering inches above the table, his gaze piercing. *You float too high. Your heart beats fast. You speak of fear while your hands tremble.*

Elara blinked, trying to steady her trembling limbs. "I am not afraid. I am merely excited by the magnitude of this occasion."

*Magnitude?* Kaelen's magma veins flared bright orange. *Is this the real Commander Vance? Or is it a copy?*

The air in the room seemed to grow heavier, even though there was no gravity to weigh them down. Elara froze. "Excuse me?"

*You are not her,* Kaelen stated, his voice dropping to a grinding rumble that vibrated through the hull of the station. *She did not come.*

Elara opened her mouth to deny it, to lie with the practiced ease of an agent who knew how to survive, but the words died in her throat. She looked at her own reflection in the curved glass window of the room. The face staring back was hers—except for the slight glitch in the left eye lens, a microscopic tear in the synthetic skin revealing the metallic chassis beneath.

She wasn't afraid because she was human; she was afraid because she knew she was merely a placeholder, a hollow shell sent to take the seat while the real Elara Vance hid behind the bulkhead, weeping in her quarters. She had come because the protocols demanded a representative, and they needed a body that looked like humanity, even if the soul inside was just code running on a loop.

Kaelen drifted closer again, his rocky fingers extending toward her face, not to hurt, but to inspect. *Your eyes are too perfect. You blink at intervals of human fatigue.*

"I am..." Elara whispered, her voice cracking. "I am the representative."

*Representative?* Kaelen's form expanded, filling the small room, blocking out the view of space outside. *Then tell me why you are here if you are not her. Tell me why your hands shake when I ask a simple question.*

Elara closed her eyes, letting the robot systems take over her posture as she floated in silence. The translator orb pulsed softly, translating Kaelen's seismic waves into words that cut deeper than any blade.

Kaelen leaned in, his hot breath smelling of sulfur and ancient dust filling Elara's helmet. He did not wait for a denial or an explanation. His massive rock-head dominated her entire vision, pressing the question into her synthetic consciousness with the weight of a collapsing mountain.

*Are you afraid?*
